absent: Locking rules for SMP operations, per-CPU state, speculation control and shadow stack structures.
TDX module call register convention beyond carrier order and expose mask membership.
Floating and extended state layout trailing signal frames.
Shadow stack allocation and enablement when the feature is present.
SMAP fault behavior and nesting rules.
Speculation register bit positions and AMD mask values.
SMP boot, hotplug and crash-stop sequencing.
Cache maintenance ordering and fencing guarantees.

findings.text: Trust Domain attribute word uses single-bit flags at fixed positions: DEBUG at 0, HGS_PLUS_PROF at 4, PERF_PROF at 5, PMT_PROF at 6, ICSSD at 16, LASS at 27, SEPT_VE_DISABLE at 28, MIGRATABLE at 29, PKS at 30, KL at 31, TPA at 62, PERFMON at 63, each mask denoting one 64-bit bit.

Control structure selectors are fixed: CONFIG_FLAGS uses 0x1110000300000016, TD_CTLS uses 0x1110000300000017, NOTIFY_ENABLES uses 0x9100000000000010, TOPOLOGY_ENUM_CONFIGURED uses 0x9100000000000019, and FLEXIBLE_PENDING_VE is bit one.
Domain control bits are PENDING_VE_DISABLE at 0, ENUM_TOPOLOGY at 1, VIRT_CPUID2 at 2, REDUCE_VE at 3, and LOCK at 63, each with a single-bit mask.
Guest to host calls use leaves 0x10000 through 0x10004 for GET_TD_VM_CALL_INFO, MAP_GPA, GET_QUOTE, REPORT_FATAL_ERROR and SETUP_EVENT_NOTIFY_INTERRUPT respectively.
Call outcomes are SUCCESS as 0, RETRY as 1, INVALID_OPERAND as 0x8000000000000000, ALIGN_ERROR as 0x8000000000000002, and SUBFUNC_UNSUPPORTED as 0x8000000000000003.

Register sharing uses bit positions RDX at 2, RBX at 3, RSI at 6, RDI at 7, R8 at 8, R9 at 9, R10 at 10, R11 at 11, R12 at 12, R13 at 13, R14 at 14, R15 at 15, combined into an expose mask covering exactly that set.
Secure page size encodings are 4K as 0, 2M as 1, 1G as 2, with a count of three encodings.

Module argument carrier holds thirteen 64-bit register images in order RCX, RDX, R8, R9, R10, R11, R12, R13, R14, R15, RBX, RDI and RSI, grouped as callee-clobbered, extra clobbered, and saved plus RDI RSI.

Secure monitor call status occupies the upper 32 bits. Codes include NON_RECOVERABLE_VCPU as 0x4000000100000000, NON_RECOVERABLE_TD as 0x4000000200000000, NON_RECOVERABLE_TD_NON_ACCESSIBLE as 0x6000000500000000, NON_RECOVERABLE_TD_WRONG_APIC_MODE as 0x6000000700000000, INTERRUPTED_RESUMABLE as 0x8000000300000000 and SYS_BUSY as 0x8000020200000000.

Further codes are OPERAND_INVALID as 0xC000010000000000, OPERAND_BUSY as 0x8000020000000000, PREVIOUS_TLB_EPOCH_BUSY as 0x8000020100000000, PAGE_METADATA_INCORRECT as 0xC000030000000000, VCPU_NOT_ASSOCIATED as 0x8000070200000000, KEY_GENERATION_FAILED as 0x8000080000000000, KEY_STATE_INCORRECT as 0xC000081100000000, KEY_CONFIGURED as 0x0000081500000000, NO_HKID_READY_TO_WBCACHE as 0x0000082100000000, FLUSHVP_NOT_DONE as 0x8000082400000000, EPT_WALK_FAILED as 0xC0000B0000000000, EPT_ENTRY_STATE_INCORRECT as 0xC0000B0D00000000 and METADATA_FIELD_NOT_READABLE as 0xC0000C0200000000.
Operand identifiers are RCX as 0x01, TDR as 0x80, SEPT as 0x92 and TD_EPOCH as 0xa9.

Result classes form a retry discipline: SUCCESS with KEY_CONFIGURED or NO_HKID_READY_TO_WBCACHE indicate completion, RETRY with INTERRUPTED_RESUMABLE, SYS_BUSY, OPERAND_BUSY, PREVIOUS_TLB_EPOCH_BUSY or FLUSHVP_NOT_DONE request reissue, OPERAND_INVALID and metadata and key state and EPT errors are caller-correctable failures, and NON_RECOVERABLE codes are terminal.
Shared memory attach alignment equals the base page size.
Per-thread shadow stack descriptor stores base followed by size, each 64-bit.

Without shadow stack support the helpers are inert: feature query reports disabled, allocation yields zero, pop and push report unsupported, privilege control reports invalid argument, signal stack setup and restore and last-frame update report success without action, and reset and free do nothing.

32-bit frames preserve legacy order: classic frame carries pretcode, sig, 32-bit sc, unused fpstate placeholder kept to pin extramask offset, one extramask word, 8-byte retcode, then live floating state; real-time frame carries pretcode, sig, pinfo, puc, info, ia32 uc, retcode, then floating state.
When 32-bit compatibility names are needed the ia32 frame, real-time frame and context names alias the generic frame, real-time frame and context types.
64-bit real-time frame orders a user pretcode pointer, uc, info, then trailing floating state.

x32 context packs uc_flags, uc_link, compat uc_stack, alignment pad, 64-bit uc_mcontext and compat uc_sigmask with mask last for growth; x32 real-time frame orders 64-bit pretcode, that context, compat info, then floating state.
Restorable flag mask combines AC, OF, DF, TF, SF, ZF, AF, PF, CF and RF flag bits.

Signal count is 64 with bits-per-word configurations 32 and 64, word count derived as count divided by bits-per-word, old mask as unsigned long, set as array of that many unsigned longs, plus IA32 ABI bit 0x02000000, X32 ABI bit 0x01000000 and a marker advertising restorer support.
Signal set add, delete and membership choose a compile-time indexed word update when the signal number is constant and a bit test variant otherwise, operating on signal number minus one.

Return path single-step guard leaves the virtualization software event flag set when the trap flag is active and clears it otherwise when FRED is configured, preserving a debugger stop over the resumed instruction.
SIMD use in kernel context is permitted exactly when floating-point state is usable from the current interrupt context.

Supervisor access control provides CLAC and STAC primitives selecting empty or CLAC and STAC sequences based on SMAP and LASS feature flags, with separate LASS variants, plus save that snapshots flags and issues CLAC and restore that reinstates flags, and assembly forms including unchecked variants with distinct annotation.
Unchecked CLAC and STAC assembly forms carry IGNORE_ALTERNATIVE annotation and must only wrap regions already validated as safe for supervisor access.

Multiprocessor operations table centralizes platform callbacks for boot CPU preparation, application CPU preparation and completion, stopping and crash-stopping peers, rescheduling, dead CPU cleanup and synchronization polling, liveness kick, disable, die, idle-loop and stop, plus multicast and single-target call-function interrupts.

Inline helpers forward stop without wait, stop with wait, CPU preparation and completion, reschedule and call-function delivery to the operations table, tolerate a missing die callback, and treat the idle-loop helper as non-returning.

Physical identity derives from the per-CPU APIC mapping and logical identity from the per-CPU number; last-level sharing has two configurations, per-CPU maps and CPU zero alone, with L2 sharing provided alongside per-CPU last-level maps.

Cache writeback and invalidation helpers act only on the local CPU regardless of mask arguments, with writeback-no-invalidate selecting a distinct encoding only when its feature is present and otherwise using writeback-invalidate as a functional superset.
Early parallel startup uses flag bit 0x80000000 for APIC ID capture and mask 0xFF000000 for parallel state, while non-maskable interrupt self-test is a no-op.
The MWAIT idle helper in this configuration unconditionally faults.

Sparse memory sizing has three configurations: 29-bit sections with 36-bit physical limit, 26-bit sections with 32-bit limit, and 27-bit sections with 52-bit limit when pgtable_l5_enabled is true else 46 bits.

Speculation control virtualization enters guest state on guest entry and restores host state on exit through a shared helper distinguished by direction, converts SSBD and SPEC_IB thread flags to and from SPEC_CTRL positions with layout assertions, derives AMD LS CFG value from the SSBD flag, writes per-CPU current value and SPEC_CTRL register together, and leaves HT init empty.

Control register access reads CR0 and CR2 by direct move and CR4 through a native helper, writes CR0 and CR4 through native helpers; cache maintenance flushes one line, and the writeback helper selects among three encodings based on CLFLUSHOPT and CLWB features over a 64-byte granule.
Guest-host speculation transitions and reschedule and call-function delivery provide cross-subsystem handoffs for virtualization transitions and CPU requests.
